hookSwap.$comment: The placeValue4Digit hook asserted something a Sri Lankan child knows is false. Books here cost 3-digit prices, so 'book prices are four-digit numbers' is wrong on the facts — and a hook that opens on something the child can see is untrue costs more than a weak hook does. A school bag genuinely runs to four digits. Round 2's logic fix is kept: what makes the number readable is knowing where its digits sit, not how many there are. Both sentences stay under 14 words.

softenToSoftCheck.$comment: Half the authored ASKs become SOFT_CHECKs. An ASK stops the lesson, opens the mic for a judged answer and runs an 8s/12s/10s silence ladder into FEEDBACK or RETEACH; a SOFT_CHECK opens the mic for 3s, warmly acknowledges any sound, and flows on unjudged. The script asked one judged question every 35s, so a 12-minute sitting carried ~21 of them. Every beat kept below is a real checkpoint; every beat here is a repeat of the checkpoint before it, or a question that answers itself, or one that cannot be judged at all. Beat TYPE and pauseType both change; the words are untouched.

neutralConfirmation.$comment: ROUND 4, THE SYSTEMIC ONE. The runtime already plays a praise or a miss clip based on what the child actually said (AUTHORED_LINES.feedbackCorrect / feedbackWrong, chosen by the planner). A scripted beat that ALSO congratulates therefore congratulates unconditionally — it plays word for word after a wrong answer, after a retry, and after silence that ended in Zara demonstrating the answer herself. Every beat that follows a question is now a NEUTRAL statement of the answer, which is true in all three cases. The praise did not go away; it moved to the only place that knows whether it is deserved.

authoringRule.$comment: ROUND 4, for every future lesson. Added to the author's prompt (scripts/author-script.ts) so this class of bug is not written again.
authoringRule.rule: The beat following any question is a neutral statement of the answer. Never write praise or a verdict into a scripted beat; the runtime supplies praise and miss lines based on the real answer.

validatorAudit.$comment: ROUND 4. What the two new rules found across all beats, and what was done about each.

noAssumedAnswer.action: NONE — all three were false positives, and the rule was narrowed instead. Each follows a SOFT_CHECK that ends on a rhetorical tag ('කූරු හතරේ පිළිවෙළ ඔයාට මතක හිටියා නේද?'), which is a confirmation rather than an invitation to produce a number; the number that follows is Zara choosing her own example, not assuming the child's. The rule now fires only on a question that actually asks the child to make something — 'ඔයා කැමති', or no expectedAnswer AND no rhetorical tag.

restoredPrompt.$comment:
ROUND 6. Round 4's neutral-confirmation rewrite of readWrite4Digit:3 removed its second half — the question that asked for the NEXT number's name — because a beat following a question must be a statement. That was right about the praise and wrong about the question: :4 was left explaining the silent zero in 101, a number the lesson had stopped naming. The question comes back as its own beat, where it should have been all along.

සංඛ්‍යා නාමය went with it. That term is not like සංඛ්‍යාංකය, which both native reviewers struck deliberately as bookish — it is the name of the thing this entire concept teaches, and it disappeared by accident. It is reintroduced in the run the guide introduces it in ('have students read each number's name aloud').

visualContinuity.$comment: ROUND 7 — the third native review: the script 'holds together conversationally'; what remained was the board. Two facts first. (1) At runtime a beat with board 'none' has ALWAYS inherited the previous board — stageBeatBoard returns nothing for it and the runtime only repaints on a staged board — so no beat below changed its runtime meaning. What changed is that 'none' is now DOCUMENTED as inherit, the review doc prints what is inherited instead of the word 'none', and blanking on purpose has its own word, {kind:'clear'}, which this script uses nowhere: both concept boundaries land on a title card, which replaces the board outright, and a clear before it would be the exact flash the new validator forbids. (2) No content_bank ExpansionExercise row contains 5421, so :96 stages a synthetic one.

phraseRubrics.$comment: Round 10. Phrase answers (CHECK_MY_WORK, verbal why-questions) were string-matched against one phrase, so a child saying the finding in other words was marked wrong. A rubric per beat: judged first by a deterministic token match after number-name normalisation, then — only if nothing matches — by one Flash call with the rubric. After one miss the three `choices` are offered as taps (the correct finding first; the runtime shuffles).

modes.$comment: Round 10. Mastery stars never landed because authored beats carried no teaching mode, and the orchestrator counts only mode-3 answers as unaided. Modes are now assigned at build time (authoredScript.toRuntimeBeats) from the beat's role: demonstrations and every non-asking beat → 1; an ASK inside a guided run (the abacus build, the card reading, the 999 + 1 build-up) → 2; a standalone ASK in the concept's closing guide steps (the last two of the concept), the closing exercise, and CHECK_MY_WORK → 3. Recorded here because it changes how the lesson judges mastery, not the words.

chipWording.$comment: ANSWER-MODE ROUND. Every question now has a touch surface; speech is offered on all and required on none. touchOnly.$comment: TOUCH-ONLY ROUND. No authored beat changed its words. The change is how the child answers: every ASK/SOFT_CHECK/CHECK_MY_WORK is answered by touch and judged on the device; the microphone opens only in the ✋ chat. Script-adjacent: (1) readAloud beats (readWrite4Digit:2, :3a, :15; placeValue4Digit:58, :62) now run as reading practice before their chips — a 3 s 'කියන්න බලන්න' pause with a faint 🎤 cue (nothing recorded), then Zara reads the number herself with the new recorded frame 'මම කියන්නම් —' + the composed number; (2) every SOFT_CHECK is a 2 s pause where a tap counts as engagement — the 'හරි!' acknowledgement clip is no longer played; (3) three lines join src/lib/authoredLines.ts for the actor to record: readBack 'මම කියන්නම් —', touchNudge 'ඕනෑම එකක් තෝරලා බලන්න.' (the one nudge at 12 s of no tap; at 25 s she demonstrates), micPermission 'ඔයාගේ කටහඬ අහන්න මට අවසර ඕනේ. හරි කියලා දෙන්නකෝ.' (said before the browser asks, on the first ✋). Until recorded, these three are read on the board rather than rendered. The voice silence ladder (wait / offerHelp / giveUpReveal) and confirmHeard stay only for the opt-in reading assessment (VOICE_ASSESSMENT=on).

coverage.$comment: Coverage round (docs/qa/session1-triage.md, cluster C — issues 6c, 11, 22, 25; plus item 3's five builds), 16 Sep 2026. The script asked a SAMPLE of each exercise; the child, the parent and the guide expect all of it. Every number in the list is asked (84, 101, 528, 997 — read-aloud), every blank of the numeral ↔ name table is filled (six: rows alternate Zara / child per MODE 2), all five builds of the digit puzzle are asked, and the big place-value table (7b58e436, 15 blanks) is ONE atomic exercise at the close of placeValue4Digit: Zara demonstrates row 1 cell by cell (2 · දහසස්ථානය · 1000 · 2000), then the 15 blanks of rows 2–6 alternate child / Zara, a neutral confirmation after each of the child's. Frame lines are reused where one exists (the :3a / :30c / :30b / :18e / :18g frames verbatim; AUTHORED_LINES.askBlank for every table question; the builder's revealBlank frame for Zara's fills) — the only new words carry the cell's own value, and a native speaker should read them in session-1-original.md. :52 no longer stages the table it never worked. Applied last; overrides every earlier round it touches (:5's softening, the ending round's :102–:108).
